analysis: The PR only changes docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and one added row in the Failure modes table (head line 3552). The row documents a provider crash loop on pre-release macOS 27.2 builds caused by SDK 27.2 back-deployed Date `>=`/`<=` operators, plus the mitigations: `scripts/check-date-comparisons.py`, `scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py`, and rewriting comparisons with `timeIntervalSince(_:)`. No executable code, configuration, protocol, key handling, attestation, or cache code changed, so there is no change to the provider's trust boundaries or the T-041 prefix-cache posture. The two units are head-text excerpts of the same doc, and the remaining text (MiMo, cluster, Qwen, invariants) is unchanged context. The added row asserts that the cluster service's timed checks (memory replan, member sync, update and approval checks, restart backoff, manifest repair deadline) keep their thresholds after the change. That is a claim about source I cannot see; the source edits to ClusterService.swift and ClusterModelProvisioningStore.swift are not in this batch. If those edits changed timing or deadline behavior, availability (T-043-style watchdog, T-057) could be affected. The doc itself indicates semantics are preserved, so I raise no finding. Remaining integration question: whether the Swift source changes behind this doc row are semantically equivalent, and whether the Release Integrity checks are actually wired into the release lane. Neither is verifiable from the supplied evidence, so this is noted as a coverage limit, not a defect. No threat-model update is needed from this PR.
